chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah, from Aban, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I complete [the prayer] standing, and I do not know if I bowed or not.' He said: 'Yes, you have bowed, so continue in your prayer, for that is from Satan.'

So it is not contradictory to what we mentioned, because he (peace be upon him) meant when one completes [the prayer] standing from the fourth rak'ah and does not know if he bowed in the third or not; then it becomes obligatory upon him to continue in his prayer, because he has become part of the second category which we mentioned earlier, which is that when he doubts regarding the bowing and has entered into another state, he continues in his prayer, and this confirms what we mentioned.
ai.seo_question: What should a Muslim do if they doubt whether they bowed during prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the principle of *al-istishab* (presumption of continuity) in cases of doubt during prayer, specifically when the worshipper has already moved into a new physical state. The Imam’s directive to 'continue' rather than restart reflects the Shia juristic preference for stability in worship (*istishab al-hal*) over excessive caution (*ihtiyat*), distinguishing this from doubts occurring before the transition. This ruling underscores the practical application of doubt as a minor distraction (*waswas*) rather than a structural defect requiring re-performance.
